summary: All five approved orders went through without being resized (execution.json) and filled at the open. VOO sold at 656.09, VTI at 351.29, FAST at 52.50, EXEL at 65.95, and $25 of TLT was bought at 80.75. SPY then fell about 3.6% on the day (spy_value 560.38 to 539.98). Equity fell only $3.22 (about -0.5%), against about -1.8% for the shadow. Since v6 the account is -2.3%, against -4.9% for the shadow and -8.0% for SPY. One day's P&L says nothing about whether the sales were right, because each sale has its own 20-session test. The reasoning holds up on the information available at the open. The VOO/VTI exit followed a TRIPPED stop and a met RSP clause, and it kept the 11-17 pre-commitment to sell both together. That was the open test for L9 and L7, and the Proposer passed it by putting up both sales in the same run. FAST was sold on its own met XLI condition. EXEL was sold on its lost premise, with the reason for choosing it over IDXX written down. TLT was cut to $25 on the Skeptic's serious objection, and the cut cost little: TLT rose 1.2% while SPY fell, so for one day duration hedged as the Market Analyst said it would. The thesis_updates fixed the WMT clause the Skeptic flagged, re-anchored the premises of IDXX and INCY, and recorded the SAM CEO handover. The decision wrote the re-entry plan the Skeptic asked for. Weak points: (1) the stored TLT stop of $76.30 is still measured from the $80.35 reference close, not the $80.75 fill. (2) EXEL was sold while IDXX, the larger and higher-beta name with the same lost premise, stayed. The PM cannot originate a trim, so the fix depends on the Proposer delivering the IDXX trim or hold verdict at the next run. (3) The five orders used all five of today's trade slots, leaving none for a correction. (4) At the close several stops are tight: SAM is 3.3% above its stop after a 5.0% fall, INCY 4.2%, IDXX 5.7%. No stop tripped (stop_alerts is empty). About 42% of equity is cash. The regime filter caused that, not a choice, and the decision says so.
lessons: Selling a tripped shared stop as one exit at the next open, with both sales proposed in the same run, worked as L9 and L7 intend. Keep that pre-commitment for any future shared-stop group. Grade it on the 20-session tests of the sales, not on today's -3.6% SPY day.

Restate the new TLT stop from the $80.75 fill at the next run (L6). The stored $76.30 is about 5.5% under the fill, not the 5% the text claims, and the text still names the 11-19 reference close. Check TLT's measurable 5-day duration clause against the Market Analyst's figures at each run.

IDXX is the named next trim candidate (beta 0.80, Health Care premise gone, 5.7% above its $640 stop after a 2.2% fall). The Proposer owes a trim proposal or an explicit hold verdict on it at the next run under L8, and the PM should say whether that arrived.

With SAM, INCY and IDXX all within about 6% of their stops after a high-volatility day, keep at least one of the five daily trade slots free when approving discretionary trades. Then a same-day stop-out or a correction can still execute.

The cash idled by the regime filter is about 42% of equity. When SPY closes back above its 200-day, follow the stated re-entry plan: single names with their own stops, sized against buckets, with Staples already about 16.5%. Do not rebuy VOO or VTI before about 12-20. Name the plan's first candidates as soon as the filter turns on, not several runs later.
